objectives.text: Singers arrive at rehearsal with their parts ready
The choir spends no weekly volunteer effort keeping the service running

rejected.label: Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app
rejected.note: Stated as a must. Read as a way of putting the right parts in front of singers for each rehearsal, so judged through part-finding. Whether it is a hard requirement is asked in questions.

anchors.text: A source states that a singer must search or browse the whole library to find a part for a rehearsal.
A source states that a singer can open their own parts from a personal folder or part view, but must look up a rehearsal's music by name.
A source states that a singer can open the part for a given rehearsal in one step from a personal folder or part view.

definition.objective: Singers arrive at rehearsal with their parts ready
definition.question: How many steps does a singer take to open their own part for a given rehearsal?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation or a product page describing how a singer reaches a part; a reviewer's general praise of the app does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a singer reaches a part.
Sources disagree on the steps a singer must take.

exclusions: How the library is filled or kept up to date; that is volunteer-upkeep.
Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app: judge the steps a singer takes to the part, not the sync mechanism.

anchors.text: A source states that a volunteer must update the library, accounts or files every week.
A source states that a volunteer must do a recurring task, but on a longer interval than weekly.
A source states that the service needs no volunteer task on any recurring schedule.

definition.objective: The choir spends no weekly volunteer effort keeping the service running
definition.question: How often, and how much, must a volunteer keep the service going?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of what someone must do to keep the library, accounts or files current; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes what upkeep the service needs.

exclusions: How well the library works once it is kept up to date; that is part-finding.
The price of the service.

provenance.quote: Singers need to find their parts quickly before rehearsal.
We can't afford anything that needs a volunteer to maintain it every week.

questions: You said the service must sync with the rehearsal calendar app. Is that a hard requirement, so that a service without it is ruled out whatever else it does? It is treated here as a way of getting singers to their parts, which you have not confirmed.
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
All three services advertise colour themes (dark mode, or light and dark). Does that matter to you?
FolioSing advertises offline mode. Do singers need their parts when there is no signal at rehearsal?

objectives.text: Mentors give their evenings to building, not to chasing orders

rejected.label: Ordered through the school's purchase-order system
rejected.note: Stated as a must, with no reason given. Read here as a way of keeping order handling off the mentors, so judged through mentor-chasing. This reading is unconfirmed and is asked in questions.

rejected.label: Branding
rejected.note: The user dismissed it: Forget about branding, we don't care.

criteria.label: Days for a stocked part to arrive

anchors.text: A source states that stocked items arrive five or more working days after ordering.
A source states that stocked items arrive within two to four working days of ordering.
A source states that stocked items arrive the next working day after ordering.

definition.question: How many working days after ordering does a stocked part reach the school?
definition.evidenceRule: The supplier's own delivery terms or product page stating a delivery or dispatch time; a reviewer's general praise of speed does not count.

missingRules.when: No source states a delivery time for stocked parts.
Sources give conflicting delivery times for the same item.

exclusions: Stock range: how many items the supplier carries.
The shipping price.

anchors.text: A source states that a mentor must check each order and chase it by hand when it is late or incomplete.
A source states that a buyer can track orders online, but a late or incomplete order must be chased by a person.
A source states that late or incomplete orders are reported to the buyer without a person chasing them.

definition.objective: Mentors give their evenings to building, not to chasing orders
definition.question: After an order is placed, what must a person do by hand to get it?
definition.evidenceRule: The supplier's documentation of order tracking, notifications and what the buyer must do for a late or missing item; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes what a buyer must do after placing an order.
Sources conflict on whether a late order is reported to the buyer.

exclusions: Ordered through the school's purchase-order system: judge the mentor time after ordering, not the ordering route.
Delivery speed: that is delivery-time.

provenance.quote: We need parts to arrive before competition deadlines.
Mentors are volunteers and can't spend evenings chasing orders.

questions: Everything has to be ordered through the school's purchase-order system. Is that a hard requirement, so that a supplier that cannot take purchase orders is ruled out whatever else it does? It is treated here as a way of keeping order handling off the mentors, which you have not said.
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget? Servo Shed advertises bulk discounts.
BotParts Direct advertises school accounts. Does that matter to you, or is it how the purchase-order requirement would be met?
All three advertise loyalty points or rewards. Does that matter to you?

objectives.text: Members borrow a tool without waiting days
Shared tools are not lost or forgotten

rejected.label: Mobile app
rejected.note: Stated as a need, with no reason given. Read here as a way for members to request a tool quickly, so judged through time-to-borrow. Unconfirmed; asked in questions whether it is a hard requirement.

rejected.label: Knowing who has which tool
rejected.note: Read as a way of keeping tools from going missing. The outcome that matters is whether an overdue tool can be followed up to its member, so that is the criterion.

criteria.label: Wait to borrow an available tool

anchors.text: A source states that a request is approved by a person, and collection is arranged days later.
A source states that a member can request a tool online, and collection is arranged on a set day each week.
A source states that a member can borrow an available tool the same day it is requested.

definition.objective: Members borrow a tool without waiting days
definition.question: How long must a member wait to borrow a tool that is available?
definition.evidenceRule: The service's documentation of how borrowing requests are handled and when collection happens; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a borrowing request is handled.

exclusions: Mobile app: judge how long a member waits, not the device used to request.
Lent tools can be followed up: that is a different question, about who holds a tool.

criteria.label: Lent tools can be followed up

anchors.text: A source states that a lent tool is recorded only as lent, with no member name attached.
A source states that a lent tool is recorded against the borrowing member, and the record is cleared by hand on return.
A source states that the holder of every lent tool can be shown at any time, with the date it was lent.

definition.objective: Shared tools are not lost or forgotten
definition.question: If a lent tool is not back when due, can the society find which member has it?
definition.evidenceRule: The service's documentation of how lending is recorded and what can be looked up; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how lent tools are recorded.
Sources disagree on whether the holder of a tool can be looked up.

exclusions: Knowing who has which tool: judge whether an overdue tool can be traced to its member, not how the record is kept.
Wait to borrow an available tool: that is time-to-borrow.

provenance.quote: Members should be able to borrow a tool without waiting days.
We want to know who has which tool so nothing goes missing.

questions: You said it needs a mobile app. Is that a hard requirement, so that a service without one is ruled out whatever else it does? It is treated here as a way for members to borrow quickly, which you have not said.
The brochures differ on the number of languages supported (14, 9 and 20). Do your members need more than one language?
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
Do you need to know who borrowed a tool before, as well as who has it now?

objectives.text: Walkers know the route before the walk
Walkers can follow the route on the walk

rejected.label: Exports GPX files
rejected.note: Stated as a must, with no reason given. Read here as a way of getting the route onto a device for the walk, so judged through route-on-walk. Unconfirmed; asked in questions.

rejected.label: Social feed
rejected.note: The user dismissed it: Nobody cares about the social feed.

criteria.label: Sharing a route with the group in advance

anchors.text: A source states that a route can only be shared as a file or link that the leader sends to each person.
A source states that a route can be shared with a group, but members must accept an invitation before they can see it.
A source states that a leader can share a route with a named group, and members see it without an extra step.

definition.objective: Walkers know the route before the walk
definition.question: What must a walker do before they can see a route the leader shared?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of how a route is shared and what members must do to see it; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a route is shared with a group.
Sources disagree on what members must do to see a shared route.

exclusions: Taking a route onto a navigation device for the walk: that is route-on-walk.

criteria.label: Route can be followed on the walk

anchors.text: A source states that a route can only be viewed inside the app, with no way to take it onto another device.
A source states that a route can be taken onto another device, but only after a conversion step.
A source states that a route can be loaded straight into a navigation device or app and followed on the walk.

definition.objective: Walkers can follow the route on the walk
definition.question: Can a route be taken onto a device the leader uses on the walk, and in how many steps?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of how a route leaves the app; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a route leaves the app.
Sources conflict on whether a route can be taken onto a device.

exclusions: Exports GPX files: judge whether a route can be followed on the walk, not the file format.
Sharing a route with the group in advance: that is route-sharing.

provenance.quote: Leaders need to share a route with the group the evening before.

questions: You said it has to export GPX files. Is that a hard requirement, so that a route app which cannot export GPX is ruled out whatever else it does? And what is the file for: a navigation device, another app, or something else? The criterion route-on-walk is my guess at that purpose.
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
All three advertise achievement badges. Do badges matter to the leaders at all?
TrailMark advertises offline maps and PathPost a weather overlay. Do the leaders need either when there is no signal on the walk, or for planning?

objectives.text: Parents buy their tickets with little effort
Each seat is sold to one buyer only
Late buyers can get a ticket on the night

rejected.label: Takes card payments at the door
rejected.note: Stated as a must, with no reason given. Read here as a way of selling tickets on the night, so judged through door-sales. Unconfirmed; asked in questions.

rejected.label: Merchandise sales
rejected.note: The user dismissed it: Don't bother with merchandise sales.

criteria.label: Steps to buy a ticket online

anchors.text: A source states that buying a ticket needs an account to be created first, or takes several separate pages.
A source states that a ticket can be bought without an account, over more than one page.
A source states that a ticket can be bought without an account on a single page.

definition.objective: Parents buy their tickets with little effort
definition.question: How many pages, and how much sign-up, does a parent need before a ticket is paid for?
definition.evidenceRule: The service's own description of the purchase process or a product page; a reviewer's praise of speed does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a ticket is bought online.
Sources disagree on whether an account is needed to buy.

exclusions: Seats being sold twice: that is seat-locking.
Tickets sold at the door: that is door-sales.

anchors.text: A source states that seats are not assigned, so two buyers can be sold the same seat.
A source states that seat assignment is shown on the sale page, but a seat can be held by two buyers until the sale is confirmed.
A source states that a seat is locked to one buyer as soon as it is chosen, and cannot be sold again for that performance.

definition.objective: Each seat is sold to one buyer only
definition.question: Can the service stop two buyers being sold the same seat for one performance?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's description of how seats are assigned and held; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how seats are assigned or held.
The performance has no assigned seats, such as a standing-only event.

exclusions: Tickets sold at the door: that is door-sales.
Steps to buy a ticket online: that is purchase-time.

criteria.label: Tickets can be sold at the door

anchors.text: A source states that tickets can only be bought online before the performance.
A source states that tickets can be bought at the door on the night, but a sale there needs a separate setup the box office must arrange in advance.
A source states that a ticket can be bought at the door on the night from the same service that sells online tickets.

definition.objective: Late buyers can get a ticket on the night
definition.question: Can a ticket be sold to someone at the door on the night?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of door or box office sales; a reviewer's praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes sales on the night.
Sources disagree on whether a ticket can be sold at the door.

exclusions: Takes card payments at the door: judge whether a ticket can be sold on the night, not the payment method.
Seats being sold twice: that is seat-locking.

provenance.quote: Parents should be able to buy tickets in under a minute.
We are sick of double-booked seats.

questions: You said it has to take card payments at the door. Is that a hard requirement, so that a service without it is ruled out whatever else it does? The criterion door-sales, that late buyers can get a ticket on the night, is my guess at the purpose.
Cost was not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
All three advertise colour themes. Does that matter to you?
BoxOffice Lite advertises a door scanning app. Do you need tickets checked at the door, and would that help with double-booked seats?
